text:
Marta (Product): FYI — CascadePay filed an urgent ticket: p95 latency jumped ~3x since last night's Optimize rollout. Support ticket #2457. Customer on Dedicated capacity, high SLA. Can we triage?

Rebecca (Support): CascadePay says chat completions p95 ~1600ms (was ~450ms). They attached traces and request IDs. I forwarded logs to eng oncall.

Samir (Eng Runtime): On it. Any chance this coincides with the "optimize:dynamic-batching" flag flip we rolled at 23:07? deploy-bot showed the rollout finished ~23:12.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: optimize-rollout-2026-03-19-23 (id: dpl-99821) — services: runtime, router.

Toni (OnCall): I pulled metrics for cascadepay org: p50 stable, p95 up across short requests. Spike started ~23:15. No error rate increase. Looks like batching latency edge-case.

Jake (Eng Platform): Linking playbook: if batching increases tail for low-token requests we should check batching window and prefix caching behavior. Also: did the rollout change kernel selection? Samir?

Samir (Eng Runtime): Quick check: kernel pins unchanged. The new dynamic batching increases wait window up to 20ms when QPS low to improve throughput. That would not explain 1.6s. Need traces. Rebecca can you paste a request id?

Rebecca (Support): Request IDs: rq_7f3a2c, rq_7f3a9b, rq_7f4b01. Attached a cropped trace from their side: shows 1.2s in "batch_wait" and 0.3s in model. Customer is on 1xA100 dedicated.

Samir (Eng Runtime): Thanks. If batch_wait is 1.2s that's much higher than 20ms — looks like something holding the queue. Can you confirm there weren't any concurrency throttles or small node GC events? Toni, can you check node-level CPU and queued requests?

Toni (OnCall): Node metrics for pool CPAY-DEDI-1: CPU spiky at 95% at 23:14–23:18, and blocked syscalls on one pod. Also saw process OOM kill on a helper sidecar (not model server) at 23:13 that restarted. POD restart could have caused backlog.

Samir (Eng Runtime): Sidecar restart could block the router handshake until unhealthy — backlog could accumulate while we wait for health probe. That would explain 1.2s batch_wait. Need to confirm health probe timeouts.

Jake (Eng Platform): I found the probe config: readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds=5, periodSeconds=10, timeoutSeconds=1, failureThreshold=3. If the sidecar restarted, the pod would be marked unready after ~30s. That lines up.

Andrew (Solutions): CascadePay is asking for a fix and mitigation steps. Product ask: what's the customer-facing impact and what do we commit to? They want status and a timeline.

Marta (Product): Proposed immediate steps: 1) triage root cause + short-term mitigation (rollback flag or adjust probe); 2) customer comms with ETA; 3) backlog item for improved observability and resilience for sidecar failures; 4) rollout criteria update. Agree?

Samir (Eng Runtime): Agreed. Short-term mitigation: revert dynamic-batching flag for Dedicated pools or restrict it for low-concurrency orgs. I can open PR for a targeted rollback to finish in the next release train (~2 hours if no blockers).

Toni (OnCall): I can patch probe to reduce failure window on affected pool as emergency fix, but that won't address underlying sidecar crash. Recommend rollback of optimize flag + investigate sidecar memory leak.

Jake (Eng Platform): I'll create a dedicated alert rule to detect sustained batch_wait > 200ms for any dedicated pool and a dashboard tile for sidecar restarts per pool. That should be a low-effort backlog item.

Rebecca (Support): I'll send the customer an initial note: "We see increased pod restarts tied to a helper sidecar; engineering is investigating a targeted rollback and we'll update in 2 hours." Anything else to include?

Marta (Product): Add SLA impact: p95 increased from 450ms -> ~1600ms for 4% of requests. We're proposing a rollback within 2 hours and follow-up RCA. Also capture acceptance criteria for the backlog fix: ensure no single sidecar restart causes >500ms extra p95 on dedicated pools, and add circuit-breaker to bypass sidecar for routing handshake.

Andrew (Solutions): Will relay rollback plan to account team. CascadePay will want a postmortem and possibly a credit — flag for CS.

Samir (Eng Runtime): I'm opening the rollback PR and a short-runbook for oncall: adjust rollout flag via control plane to disable dynamic batching for Dedicated pools. PR: https://git.redwood/d/pl/rollback-optimize-99821 (WIP).

Toni (OnCall): Live action: I've manually drained the affected pod and set a temporary instance annotation to reduce probe sensitivity. Removing that once rollback is live.

Marta (Product): Okay we have short-term plan. Product backlog items to create (Marta assigning):
- "R1: resilience for helper sidecars" (owner: Jake) — instrument restarts, circuit-breaker, acceptance criteria above.
- "R2: rollout gating for optimize flags" (owner: Samir) — stronger canary and org-size gating.
- "R3: customer comms + compensation playbook" (owner: Rebecca/Andrew).

Rebecca (Support): Customer update sent at 00:10 UTC: "we're investigating, targeted rollback planned, update in ~2h" :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: rollout-optimizer-flag -> disabled for Dedicated pools (id: rb-4421)

Samir (Eng Runtime): Rollback applied. Monitoring now — p95 trending back to baseline for CascadePay pool. I'll keep watching for 30m.

Toni (OnCall): Confirmed. CPU stabilized, no further sidecar restarts.

Marta (Product): Thanks everyone. Next steps: Jake to open ticket for circuit-breaker/resilience; Samir to propose rollout gating checklist; Rebecca & Andrew to follow-up with customer and collect any data they need for credit request. We'll reconvene if the metrics don't normalize in 30m.

Andrew (Solutions): Noted. I'll draft an internal note for account team with timeline.

Samir (Eng Runtime): Adding final note — we should add a rollback runbook to rollout docs so CS can trigger quick toggles for Dedicated pools without full deploy.

Marta (Product): Agreed. I'll add that to the backlog items. Closing thread for now, will reopen if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
